name: GoalsTable
subtitle: Yearly goals, monthly focus
promotionalText: Set goals for the year, pick a focus for each month and tick off a little work every day. Your goals stay on your device, and there is no account to make.
description:
GoalsTable keeps a year of goals in one place: what you want to get done this year, what you focus on each month, and the hours a day you actually sit down to do it.

It started as a spreadsheet of yearly plans that I kept for years, and became an app so it fits on a phone.

The year
• Goals sorted into six categories: Tech, Languages, Money, Health, Life and Projects
• A ring for how much of the year is done, and a bar for each category
• Search the year, or show only what is still open or already done

Today
• Three one-hour blocks a day to tick off as you do them
• A streak of the days you closed all three
• This month's focus, and the goals still open from it

Plan
• Twelve months, each with a short focus list picked from the year's goals
• A language and a money line for each month, if you want them

Years
• Every past year with how much of it got done
• A backlog for someday ideas, and a way to move an old goal into this year

Your data
• Your goals stay on your device. No account, no sign-up, and it works offline
• Export a backup file or a CSV whenever you like, and import the backup on another phone

The app opens with fictional sample goals, so you can see what a lived-in year looks like. Delete them or start adding your own right away.

20 languages, light and dark themes.

Privacy
Once a day the app sends anonymous usage counts: which screens and features were used, the app version, platform, language and error counts. No IDs, no goal titles and nothing you type. You can turn it off in Profile, and turning it off deletes the counts that were not sent yet. The privacy policy lists exactly what is sent.

Free, no ads.
reviewNotes:
GoalsTable is an offline tracker for yearly goals. There is no account and no sign-in. It opens on fictional sample goals, so every screen has something to show: tick a goal on Year, the daily blocks on Today, edit a month on Plan, open a past year on Years, and change the language or theme in Profile. Goals are stored on the device only.

The app makes one network call: one anonymous usage report a day to https://mrwd-metrics.vercel.app/api/ping with counts of screens and features used, the app version, platform, language and error counts. It carries no identifiers and nothing the user types. Profile > Share anonymous usage statistics turns it off. The links under More from the author open the author's website in the browser. There are no purchases and no ads.
